newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-EDP shares electrify Lisbon bourse.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EDP shares electrify Lisbon bourse.

text.p: Shares in utility group EDP-Electricidade de Portugal electrified the Lisbon exchange on Tuesday, soaring some 38 percent on their debut and giving a massive boost to overall bourse business.
EDP closed at 3,099 escudos against the 2,250 escudos at which the government floated a 30 percent share on Monday. Turnover was some 12.2 million shares.

Trade in EDP, the largest company yet to be partially privatised in Portugal, sent overall trade on the Lisbon bourse rocketing to some 65 billion escudos ($340 million), more than double the previous peak.

Traders calculated that business in EDP was equal to some 12 percent of the 101.5 million shares admitted to trade on Tuesday, adding that they expected volumes to continue heavy over coming sessions.
"EDP was the star. It was a really brilliant day," said one exhausted trader in Lisbon.

Analysts had expected that the stock, which had been heavily oversubscribed at the privatisation, would perform strongly when it was admitted to trade on Tuesday, but the result outstripped the most optimistic forecasts.
Institutional investors, who would have got far fewer shares than they bid for at the sale, were seen leading the charge for stock.
But analysts said that one of the surprising aspects of Tuesday's activity had been the huge interest of the small investor in Portugal.

"The most surprising thing about EDP was the buying that came from the retail (small investor). This did not happen at the previous privatisations," said analyst Jose Freire of Espirito Santo Research.
Analysts said that the price of 3,000 to 3,100 escudos per share could form a short-term trading range for the stock which hit a high in Lisbon on Tuesday morning of 4,050 escudos.
"I don't think that the company has room to go much above 3,200 escudos at the moment," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
"Today's close or even levels slightly below it would appear reasonable and can be maintained," said another analyst, who also declined to be identified.

Freire said that Spain's Endesa should act as a reference point for EDP, although the Portuguese company should trade at a premium because it had advanced further in the lucrative direction of telecommunications.
"There is also the expectation that profits for EDP this year could be slightly above the 91 billion escudos predicted," he added.
EDP posted a profit of 81 billion escudos in 1996.
